record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Does hypothesis (R4) hold? (Large fields existentially closed in function fields with rational place)
record.original_question: Let K be a field. A field K is called large if it is existentially closed in the power series field K((t)) in the language of rings. Hypothesis (R4) states: for an arbitrary field K, if a function field F|K (a finitely generated field extension of transcendence degree at least 1) admits a K-rational place (a valuation on F with residue field isomorphic to K), then K is existentially closed in F. It is known that local uniformization of rational places of arbitrary function fields (in all characteristics and all dimensions) implies (R4). By the work of Hironaka, local uniformization holds in characteristic 0. It is also known (Anscombe-Dittmann-Fehm 2023) that if (R4) holds, then the existential L_val(t)-theory of F_p((t)) (the formal Laurent series field over F_p in variable t, with t-adic valuation) is decidable. Does hypothesis (R4) hold in general (i.e., for all fields K and all function fields F|K with a K-rational place, is K existentially closed in F)?

artifact.category_tag: tame valued fields and large fields
artifact.self_contained_problem:
A field $K$ is called large if it is existentially closed (in the language of rings) in the formal power series field $K((t))$. A function field over $K$ is a finitely generated field extension $F\mid K$ of transcendence degree at least $1$. A $K$-rational place of $F$ is a place (equivalently, a valuation ring) of $F$ whose residue field is $K$-isomorphic to $K$.

Question: Is the following statement true? For every field $K$ and every function field $F\mid K$ that admits a $K$-rational place, the field $K$ is existentially closed in $F$ in the language of rings (i.e., every existential first-order $L_{\mathrm{ring}}$-formula with parameters from $K$ that has a solution in $F$ already has a solution in $K$).

(Equivalently: does local uniformization of rational places of arbitrary function fields, in all characteristics and dimensions, follow at the level of existential closedness?)
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open question in a recent survey on the model theory of tame valued fields. It is known to follow from local uniformization of rational places (established in characteristic 0 by Hironaka), and Anscombe–Dittmann–Fehm (2023) showed that it would imply decidability of the existential theory of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$. No proof in full generality appears in the literature.
